messages.author: 2b27719db7267c87
messages.subject: multiple imputation for multilevel data
parts:
Does anyone have experience doing multiple imputation on multilevel data?  In my case I am working with a longitudinal data set, i.e. a hierarchical data structure with two levels.  A Google search reveals that there are at least two packages that offer options for multiple imputation on two-level data, mice and pan, but I have not yet tried either package.  If anyone has successful experience doing this, I would be very curious to know what method you use.  Thanks!


Bonnie

messages.author: 2b27719db7267c87
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: multiple imputation for multilevel data
parts:
Well, I just used mice successfully, although it only seems to be able to handle missing data in one variable.  (I actually have four predictor variables with missing data, and it would be best to be able to impute all of them.)  Also, the pooled analysis results only include the fixed effects of the model, no random effects, which is unfortunate.

Thanks for the heads up about Amelia, Kristina.  I was aware of Amelia, but did not realize that it could handle multilevel data.  I will give it a try.

Bonnie

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: multiple imputation for multilevel data
parts:
OK.  I have successfully used Amelia to create five imputed data sets, and used lapply and nlme to create a multilevel model with each.  Does anyone know how to combine the five models into one final set of results in a way that makes sense for multilevel models (i.e. the final results should include both the fixed effects and the random effects)?

Bonnie
